title: They shouted “Hosanna”…
paragraphs:
They shouted “Hosanna”…
but their hearts were still negotiating with sin.

Because you can praise Jesus loudly—
and still resist Him deeply.
Here’s the tension nobody wants to admit.

The same crowd that laid down palm branches…
would later choose Barabbas over Christ.
That’s not just history.
That’s a mirror.

We celebrate the King…
as long as He doesn’t confront what we’re hiding.

We sing.
We post.
We lift our hands.
But deep inside?
There’s that quiet corner of compromise.

That habit you renamed “struggle.”
That delay you called “waiting on God.”
That pride you disguised as “discernment.”
And Jesus rides in anyway.

Not impressed.
Not intimidated.
But intentional.
Because according to Matthew 21:9, they cried, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”—which literally means “Save us now.”
But here’s the AHA moment:

They wanted saving from Rome.
Jesus came to save them from themselves.
Read that again.
The donkey wasn’t a random detail.
Zechariah 9:9 already declared it—your King would come “humble… mounted on a donkey.” Not to dominate. Not to perform. But to confront the deeper enemy: sin.
And we still miss it.

We want a Jesus who upgrades our life—
not one who crucifies our old self.

We want blessing… without surrender.
Victory… without repentance.
But Luke 19:41 says that as Jesus approached Jerusalem, He wept over it.
Think about that.

They were celebrating.
He was grieving.
Why?
Because He saw what they refused to see.

External praise.
Internal resistance.
Let me ask you something—be honest:

Are you following Jesus…
or just enjoying what He does for you?

Are you surrendered…
or just inspired?

Because there’s a kind of Christianity that looks alive on the outside
but is quietly negotiating disobedience behind the scenes.
And here’s the conviction:

You can shout “King”
and still live like you’re in control.
That’s the danger.
That’s the deception.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

If Jesus can’t correct you,
He’s not really your King—you’re just using Him.
This is where grace steps in.

Because the same Jesus who saw their shallow praise…
still rode into the city.
Still chose the cross.
Still stretched out His hands for people who didn’t fully understand Him.
Romans 5:8 says, “God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not when we got it right.
Not when our motives were pure.

While we were still mixed.
Still confused.
Still inconsistent.
That includes you.
That includes me.
He didn’t come to crush Rome.
He came to crush sin.
Yours.
Mine.
At the cross, He carried the weight of our divided hearts—our pride, our hidden compromises, our delayed obedience—and paid for it in full.
That’s the Gospel.

Not self-improvement.
Not behavior management.
A full rescue.
But here’s where it turns personal.

Grace is free—
but it is never casual.
You don’t just wave palms and walk away unchanged.
You bow.
You repent.
You surrender.

Because the same King who rides in humility…
will one day return in glory (Revelation 19:11—riding not a donkey, but a white horse).
Mercy is now.
Judgment is coming.
And the invitation is open.
Right now.
You are not called to be a fan of Jesus.
You are called to belong to Him.
IDENTITY SHIFT:

You are not a spectator in the crowd.
You are a sinner invited into sonship.

You are not defined by your hidden struggles.
You are defined by the Savior who bled for you.
So what are you going to do with Him?

Will you keep clapping…
or will you finally surrender?
If this hit something deep in you, don’t ignore it.
That’s not emotion.
That’s conviction.
Pray this in your own words:

“Jesus, I don’t want a version of You that fits my life.
I want the real You—even if it changes everything.”
This is not about hype.
This is about transformation.
Stay close. Follow if you’re ready to grow.
And next post?
We’re exposing what happened between the praise… and the betrayal.
